question: What is the main reason nurses perform mouth care for sick patients in the ward?

options.A: To stop germs from spreading to the lungs and causing serious infections
options.B: To wipe out every single normal bacteria in the mouth forever
options.C: To help arm and leg wounds heal much faster
options.D: To make sure the patient's breath smells nice for visitors

explanation: You're doing great! Keeping the mouth clean lowers the germ count, stopping bad bacteria from sliding down into the lungs or blood where they can cause serious trouble like pneumonia.

question: Why is mouth care seen as a core nursing duty rather than just making a patient look neat?

options.A: Hospital rules state that nurses must inspect teeth every morning
options.B: Dentists are almost never found inside general hospital wards
options.C: The mouth is a main doorway for germs to enter the rest of the body
options.D: Being sick always makes patients completely lose their sense of taste

explanation: Spot on! The mouth opens directly into our breathing and digestive pipes, meaning good oral care protects the whole body, not just the teeth.

question: What is the main natural job of saliva inside our mouths?

options.A: Gluing loose teeth tightly back into the jawbone
options.B: Killing off every fungus that enters through the throat
options.C: Washing away food bits and fighting off harmful acids
options.D: Bleaching tooth enamel to keep teeth sparkling white

explanation: Think of saliva as your mouth's built-in cleaning crew! It constantly washes away debris and neutralizes acids to keep your teeth safe.

question: What happens when illness or lack of water dries up the normal balance in the mouth?

options.A: Tooth enamel instantly repairs all of its own cavities
options.B: Bad bacteria multiply quickly and form dental plaque
options.C: The tongue changes its color to a bright lemon yellow
options.D: The salivary glands immediately shut down forever

explanation: When saliva drops due to sickness or dehydration, the protective shield weakens, letting nasty bacteria take over and build up as plaque.

question: Which simple tool kit helps a nurse look clearly inside a patient's mouth?

options.A: A penlight and a tongue depressor

explanation: Keep it simple and practical! A penlight gives you light, and a tongue depressor helps you gently see every corner of the oral cavity.

question: A patient on a breathing machine (ventilator) is at high risk for which mouth problem?

options.A: Losing their sense of smell completely and forever
options.B: Sudden growth of wisdom teeth right at the back
options.C: Drooling because of too much natural saliva production
options.D: Fast plaque buildup and ventilator-associated pneumonia

explanation: You've got this! Because intubated patients cannot clean their own teeth and often have dry mouths, germs gather quickly and can travel down to cause pneumonia.

question: What is the medical name for a mouth fungal infection that shows creamy white patches?
explanation: Candidiasis (often called thrush) happens when the Candida fungus grows out of control, which is common when a patient's immune system is low.

question: Why do certain long-term medications often lead to bad tooth decay?

options.A: They chemically melt away the outer shell of the teeth
options.B: They make patients crave and eat too many sugary sweets
options.C: They permanently freeze the jaw muscles so chewing stops
options.D: They cause dry mouth, taking away the protective washing power of saliva

explanation: Many drugs cause dry mouth (xerostomia). Without enough saliva to wash things away, food acids stay behind and tooth decay takes over.

question: Why must an unconscious patient be turned to their side before you clean their mouth?

options.A: To help relax the jaw so the mouth opens much wider
options.B: To push more blood straight into the gum tissues
options.C: To stop accidental choking or fluid entering the lungs
options.D: To make it easier to pull out shaky lower teeth

explanation: Safety first! Side-lying lets liquids drain safely out of the mouth instead of pooling in the throat and slipping down into the windpipe.

question: Which piece of bedside equipment is a must-have when giving mouth care to an unresponsive patient?
explanation: Unconscious patients can't spit or swallow water on their own. Having a suction machine ready is vital to clear out liquids and prevent choking.

question: Why is it smart to put a soft towel at the bottom of the sink when washing dentures?

options.A: To cushion them so they won't break if they slip and fall
options.B: To soak up extra water splashing onto your uniform
options.C: To give you a clean spot to put antiseptic cream
options.D: To keep metal pieces from scratching the shiny basin

explanation: Dentures are slippery when wet and expensive to replace! A padded sink saves the day if they accidentally drop from your hands.

question: How should removable dentures be kept when the patient is not wearing them?

options.A: Wrapped up tight in dry gauze inside a bedside drawer
options.B: In a labeled container filled with water or soaking solution
options.C: Dropped in boiling water overnight to kill all germs
options.D: Left out in the open air on top of the locker table

explanation: Keeping dentures wet in a safe container stops the plastic material from bending out of shape and keeps them ready for use.

question: What is the recommended minimum time for brushing teeth properly?
explanation: Brushing for at least two minutes gives you enough time to reach all tooth surfaces and get rid of stubborn plaque.

question: Why do nurses teach patients to use dental floss along with brushing?

options.A: To scrub the tongue and get rid of white coatings
options.B: To push fluoride paste straight down into the tooth roots
options.C: To polish the flat chewing surfaces of the back molars
options.D: To clean out food and plaque from tight spaces between teeth

explanation: Toothbrush bristles are great, but they can't squeeze into the tight spots between teeth. Flossing finishes the job for a truly clean mouth!
